violations.principle: Spec compliance — acceptance criterion not met
violations.issue: Poll loop body is empty (just `time.sleep`). No Plane polling, no `list_ready` call, no `ticket discovery: <N> ready` log output. This is an explicit acceptance criterion for this ticket that is completely unimplemented.

violations.principle: Spec compliance — acceptance criterion not met
violations.issue: No `project=<name>` in log output. Acceptance criterion requires tickets grouped by project in logs. Graph nodes and `advance_ticket` never emit project context.

`advance_ticket` function is never called from the LangGraph graph or any production code. Only called from tests. It is a second, parallel state machine that duplicates the LangGraph nodes, creating a maintenance liability when transitions change.

`NEXT_STATE` dict defines expected transitions, but each LangGraph node in `_advance` hardcodes the target state string. These can diverge. The `advance_ticket` function uses `NEXT_STATE` but the graph nodes don't. One source of truth should drive both.

`PlaneTracker.__init__` creates its own `httpx.AsyncClient` internally. Per interface-design.md ('Accept dependencies, don't create them'), the client should be injected so tests can supply a pre-configured mock or real client. Current design couples the adapter to httpx construction.

Tests mock `tracker._client` (a private internal field) instead of mocking at the system boundary (httpx module). Per mocking.md, mock at system boundaries, not internal collaborators. This creates survivable tests — they break on refactor even if behavior is unchanged.

`update_state`, `get_item`, and `add_comment` use `__all__` as a magic project slug in the Plane REST path. Plane's API specifies actual project IDs in routes. This will 404 against a real Plane instance unless the deployment has custom middleware. Also inconsistent with `list_ready` which correctly takes a project parameter.
